links.outcome: ML model discrimination compared with clinician predictions of discharge care needs
links.effect: ML one-vs-rest AUROC 0.915 [0.907 0.924], comparable to clinicians' predictions; each better for different care need types.
links.quote: The model performance (one-vs-rest AUROC = 0.915 [0.907 0.924] (95% confidence interval), is comparable to clinician's predictions of discharge care needs, despite working with only a subset of the information available to the clinician.

links.outcome: Accuracy of combined clinician-plus-machine predictions versus either alone
links.effect: Hybrid clinician-ML model achieved OVR AUROC 0.936 [0.928 0.943], more accurate than ML alone (0.915).
links.quote: Finally, we demonstrate that combining clinician and machine predictions, in a hybrid model, provides even more accurate early predictions of onward social care requirements (OVR AUROC = 0.936 [0.928 0.943]) and demonstrates the potential for human-in-the-loop decision support systems in clinical practice.

screen.reason: The study evaluates an explainable ML model predicting social care needs and tests human-in-the-loop combination (combining clinician and machine predictions vs each alone).

primary.practice: human-AI teaming / combining clinician and model predictions
